---
lang: en
format:
  typst:
    pdf-standard: ua-1
    papersize: a4
    fontsize: 9pt
    margin:
      top: 2.1cm
      bottom: 1.9cm
      left: 1.7cm
      right: 1.7cm
    mainfont: "Segoe UI"
    section-numbering: ""
brand:
  color:
    palette:
      paper: "#FFFFFF"
      ink: "#22282E"
      ink-soft: "#5C666F"
      red: "#C10016"
      blue: "#0F4C81"
    background: paper
    foreground: ink
    primary: blue
  typography:
    headings:
      weight: bold
      color: red
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    echo: false
    message: false
    warning: false
    dev: "ragg_png"
    dev.args: {bg: "white"}
    dpi: 300
    fig-width: 6.8
    fig-height: 2.5
execute:
  # A chunk that fails stops the render, so a factsheet over a lake it could
  # not read never comes out as a PDF of error messages with exit code 0.
  error: false
---

```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for a factsheet
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The one country the factsheet is about, as the repository codes it. It is
# taken from the environment variable FINCOMMONS_COUNTRY where that is set,
# so that one copy of this template renders every country:
#
#   FINCOMMONS_COUNTRY=NL quarto render esef-country-economic-factsheet.qmd
#
# Everything else -- the years, the issuers, the largest and the movers --
# follows from the lake.
report_country <- toupper(Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_COUNTRY", "AT"))

# The path to the config file, whose esef section names the Silver layer.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")

# The financial years shown, counted back from the latest the country has
# reports with facts for. A financial year is named by the calendar year it
# mostly falls in: a year ending on or before 30 June counts as the year
# before, so a year to 31 March 2026 is 2025. The sector factsheet uses the
# same rule.
n_years <- 5

# How many issuers the table of the largest shows, how many the tables of
# the movers show, and the revenue of the year before an issuer needs to be
# counted among the movers, in its own currency: a company growing from one
# million to three is not a story about the economy.
top_n <- 15
movers_n <- 8
movers_min_revenue <- 50e6

# The currency the sums are in. An issuer reporting in another currency is
# in every median and every ratio, which are free of currency, and in no
# sum, since nothing here converts.
sum_currency <- "EUR"

# The share of the best-covered year's issuers a year needs to be shown.
min_coverage <- 0.5

# How close two reports' total assets and revenue, and their equity, have to
# be for the two to be taken as the same group reported twice, by a listed
# holding and by its listed subsidiary. Heineken Holding's assets are 0.5 %
# below Heineken's, and ING Groep's revenue 0.6 % above ING Bank's; equity
# differs more, by the minorities and by what the holding holds besides.
twin_tolerance <- 0.02
twin_equity_tolerance <- 0.10

# The figures read, by concept of the IFRS taxonomy. A measure with two
# concepts takes the first where the report tags it and the second where it
# does not: revenue under IFRS 15 alone where the total is not tagged, the
# parent's share of the result or of equity where the total is not.
measures <- tibble::tribble(
  ~measure,     ~concept,                                            ~rank, ~flow,
  "revenue",    "ifrs-full:Revenue",                                     1, TRUE,
  "revenue",    "ifrs-full:RevenueFromContractsWithCustomers",           2, TRUE,
  "operating",  "ifrs-full:ProfitLossFromOperatingActivities",           1, TRUE,
  "pretax",     "ifrs-full:ProfitLossBeforeTax",                         1, TRUE,
  "profit",     "ifrs-full:ProfitLoss",                                  1, TRUE,
  "profit",     "ifrs-full:ProfitLossAttributableToOwnersOfParent",      2, TRUE,
  "staff",      "ifrs-full:EmployeeBenefitsExpense",                     1, TRUE,
  "ocf",        "ifrs-full:CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivities",      1, TRUE,
  "dividends",  "ifrs-full:DividendsPaidClassifiedAsFinancingActivities", 1, TRUE,
  "assets",     "ifrs-full:Assets",                                      1, FALSE,
  "equity",     "ifrs-full:Equity",                                      1, FALSE,
  "equity",     "ifrs-full:EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParent",          2, FALSE,
  "cash",       "ifrs-full:CashAndCashEquivalents",                      1, FALSE,
  "interest",   "ifrs-full:InterestRevenueCalculatedUsingEffectiveInterestMethod", 1, TRUE)

# The lines a bank or an insurer presents and an industrial issuer does not,
# as in the sector factsheet. A bank's revenue is interest, its balance sheet
# is its business and its margins are not a manufacturer's, so banks and
# insurers are shown on their own and kept out of the corporate figures.
#
# Interest revenue alone is not enough: a postal operator with a bank, or a
# property company with loans to its ventures, presents it too. A company
# is a bank here where its interest revenue is at least half its revenue,
# or where it tags no revenue at all; an insurer is one wherever it presents
# a line of IFRS 17.
bank_interest_share <- 0.5
financial_concepts <- c(
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceRevenue",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceContractLiabilities",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceServiceResult",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceServiceExpenses")

# The point size of the text in a chart.
chart_base_size <- 9

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The design and the libraries
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(ggplot2)
design_file <- "r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R"
design_path <- c(design_file, file.path("..", "..", "..", "templates", design_file))
design_path <- design_path[file.exists(design_path)]
if (length(design_path) == 0) {
  stop("The corporate design script ", design_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the templates directory of the package.")
}
source(design_path[1])

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(arrow)

if (!grepl("UTF-8", Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE"), ignore.case = TRUE)) {
  stop("The session does not run in a UTF-8 locale, so the names of issuers ",
       "and the typographic characters of this factsheet would print as ",
       "<U+00D6> escapes. Render with LANG=en_US.UTF-8.")
}

period_year <- function(date) {
  y <- as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  ifelse(as.integer(format(date, "%m")) <= 6L, y - 1L, y)
}

country_names <- c(
  AT = "Austria", BE = "Belgium", BG = "Bulgaria", CY = "Cyprus",
  CZ = "Czechia", DE = "Germany", DK = "Denmark", EE = "Estonia",
  ES = "Spain", FI = "Finland", FR = "France", GB = "the United Kingdom",
  GR = "Greece", HR = "Croatia", HU = "Hungary", IE = "Ireland",
  IS = "Iceland", IT = "Italy", LI = "Liechtenstein", LT = "Lithuania",
  LU = "Luxembourg", LV = "Latvia", MT = "Malta", NL = "the Netherlands",
  NO = "Norway", PL = "Poland", PT = "Portugal", RO = "Romania",
  SE = "Sweden", SI = "Slovenia", SK = "Slovakia", UA = "Ukraine")
country_name <- if (report_country %in% names(country_names))
  country_names[[report_country]] else report_country
Country_name <- paste0(toupper(substr(country_name, 1, 1)),
                       substring(country_name, 2))

short_name <- function(x, width = 40) {
  x <- gsub("Aktiengesellschaft", "AG", x, ignore.case = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Gesellschaft m\\.?b\\.?H\\.?", "GmbH", x)
  x <- gsub("Societas Europaea", "SE", x)
  x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(x))
  ifelse(nchar(x) > width, paste0(substr(x, 1, width - 1), "…"), x)
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Silver layer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)
path_silver <- yaml_paths[["esef"]][["silver"]]
if (is.list(path_silver)) path_silver <- path_silver[["path"]]
if (is.null(path_silver)) {
  stop("The config file ", config_path, " names no Silver layer for esef.")
}
for (table in c("filings", "facts")) {
  if (dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, table, "_delta_log"))) {
    stop("The ", table, " table of the esef module is a Delta table, which ",
         "this template does not read. Write the Silver layer as parquet.")
  }
}

filings <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filings")) %>%
  filter(country == report_country) %>%
  select(country, lei, filing, name, period_end, lang, processed) %>%
  collect()
if (nrow(filings) == 0) {
  countries_held <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filings")) %>%
    distinct(country) %>% collect() %>% pull(country) %>% sort()
  stop("The table of filings lists no filing of ", report_country,
       ". It lists ", paste(countries_held, collapse = ", "), ".")
}

facts_per_filing <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "facts")) %>%
  filter(country == report_country) %>%
  count(filing) %>%
  collect() %>%
  rename(facts = n)
filings <- filings %>%
  left_join(facts_per_filing, by = "filing") %>%
  mutate(facts = coalesce(facts, 0L), read = facts > 0,
         fy = period_year(period_end))
if (!any(filings$read)) {
  stop("The lake holds no facts for any filing of ", report_country, ". ",
       "Collect the reports first: esef.update_esef(spark, '<paths.yaml>', ['",
       report_country, "'], contact='<you@example.org>')")
}

latest_year <- max(filings$fy[filings$read])
report_years <- seq(latest_year - n_years + 1, latest_year)

# A year the lake holds only a few reports of is a year the pipeline was not
# asked to collect -- a report filed late, or one whose period ends early --
# and a trend through it would be a trend in what was collected. A year is
# shown where it has at least `min_coverage` of the reports of the
# best-covered year.
issuers_per_year <- filings %>% filter(read) %>% distinct(lei, fy) %>% count(fy)
covered <- issuers_per_year$fy[issuers_per_year$n >= min_coverage * max(issuers_per_year$n)]
report_years <- report_years[report_years %in% covered]
period_range <- if (length(report_years) == 1) as.character(report_years) else
  paste0(min(report_years), "–", max(report_years))

issuer_names <- filings %>%
  arrange(lei, desc(period_end), desc(processed)) %>%
  distinct(lei, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  transmute(lei, issuer = short_name(name))

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Whose report it is
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A report states the name of the entity it is the report of. Where that
# name shares nothing with the name the repository holds for the LEI it was
# filed under, and no other report filed under the LEI does either, the
# report is filed under someone else's LEI: a filing agent's test report
# filed under the agent's own, or an issuer's report filed under the LEI of
# the service that submitted it. A company that has been renamed states its
# old name in its old reports and its new one in its new, so the LEI test
# lets it pass. Such a report is left out of every figure here: its
# figures are either not real or already counted under the right LEI.
name_stop_words <- c("ag", "nv", "se", "plc", "sa", "spa", "gmbh", "kg", "bv",
                     "the", "und", "and", "for", "fur", "der", "die", "das",
                     "des", "holding", "holdings", "group", "gruppe",
                     "aktiengesellschaft", "international", "limited", "ltd",
                     "inc", "company", "beteiligungs", "europe", "european")
plain <- function(x) {
  x <- chartr("ÄÖÜäöüßÉéÈèÁáÀàÓóÍíÚúÇçÑñ", "AOUaousEeEeAaAaOoIiUuCcNn", x)
  tolower(iconv(x, to = "ASCII", sub = " "))
}
name_tokens <- function(x) {
  lapply(strsplit(gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", " ", plain(x)), " "),
         function(t) setdiff(t[nchar(t) >= 3], name_stop_words))
}
# Two names agree where a word of one is in the other, run together so that
# "LinzTextil" is "Linz Textil", or where a word of one is the initials of
# the other, so that "SBO" is "Schoeller-Bleckmann Oilfield".
names_agree <- function(a, b) {
  ta <- name_tokens(a)
  tb <- name_tokens(b)
  sa <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]", "", plain(a))
  sb <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]", "", plain(b))
  mapply(function(x, y, p, q) {
    if (length(x) == 0 || length(y) == 0) return(NA)
    ix <- paste(substr(x, 1, 1), collapse = "")
    iy <- paste(substr(y, 1, 1), collapse = "")
    any(vapply(x, function(t) grepl(t, q, fixed = TRUE), logical(1))) ||
      any(vapply(y, function(t) grepl(t, p, fixed = TRUE), logical(1))) ||
      any(startsWith(iy, x)) || any(startsWith(ix, y))
  }, ta, tb, sa, sb, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}
stated_names <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "facts")) %>%
  filter(country == report_country,
         concept == "ifrs-full:NameOfReportingEntityOrOtherMeansOfIdentification",
         is.na(dimensions), !is.na(text)) %>%
  select(filing, stated = text) %>%
  collect() %>%
  distinct(filing, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(stated = gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(stated)))
identity <- filings %>%
  select(lei, filing, name) %>%
  inner_join(stated_names, by = "filing") %>%
  mutate(agree = names_agree(name, stated)) %>%
  group_by(lei) %>%
  mutate(lei_agrees = any(agree %in% TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(agree %in% FALSE, !lei_agrees)

# One report per issuer and financial year: the one with the most facts
# and, between equals, the one the repository processed last. A correction
# or a second language of the same year is the same accounts again.
primary <- filings %>%
  filter(read, fy %in% report_years, !filing %in% identity$filing) %>%
  arrange(lei, fy, desc(period_end), desc(facts), desc(processed), filing) %>%
  distinct(lei, fy, .keep_all = TRUE)

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The figures
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

raw <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "facts")) %>%
  filter(country == report_country, concept %in% measures$concept,
         is.na(dimensions), !is.na(value)) %>%
  select(filing, lei, period_end, concept, prd_start, prd_end, unit, value) %>%
  collect() %>%
  semi_join(primary, by = "filing") %>%
  left_join(measures, by = "concept", relationship = "many-to-many")

# A report gives each figure for its own year and for the year before. The
# year before is what makes a growth rate like for like: both figures come
# from the same accounts, so a restatement or an acquisition accounted for
# in both years does not show up as growth. A flow has to cover a year, so
# that a quarter in the notes is not taken for the year; a stock has no
# start.
raw <- raw %>%
  mutate(days = as.integer(prd_end - prd_start),
         prior_end = as.Date(paste0(as.integer(format(period_end, "%Y")) - 1L,
                                    format(period_end, "-%m-%d")),
                             optional = TRUE),
         prior_end = coalesce(prior_end, period_end - 365L),
         role = case_when(prd_end == period_end ~ "current",
                          abs(as.integer(prd_end - prior_end)) <= 7 ~ "prior",
                          TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(role),
         (flow & !is.na(days) & days >= 330 & days <= 400) |
           (!flow & (is.na(prd_start) | prd_start == prd_end)))

# The currency of a report is the one most of these figures are in, and a
# figure in another is left out rather than added to it.
currency_of <- raw %>%
  filter(grepl("^iso4217:", unit)) %>%
  count(filing, unit) %>%
  arrange(filing, desc(n)) %>%
  distinct(filing, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  transmute(filing, currency = sub("^iso4217:", "", unit))

# One value per report, measure and year. A figure tagged twice with two
# values is taken as the value tagged more often, and between equals the
# larger: the statement and a note that rounds it differently agree more
# often than they disagree, and the statement is the larger.
values <- raw %>%
  inner_join(currency_of, by = "filing") %>%
  filter(unit == paste0("iso4217:", currency)) %>%
  count(filing, measure, rank, role, value, name = "times") %>%
  arrange(filing, measure, role, rank, desc(times), desc(abs(value))) %>%
  distinct(filing, measure, role, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(key = ifelse(role == "prior", paste0(measure, "_prior"), measure))

basis <- values %>%
  filter(role == "current") %>%
  select(filing, measure, rank)

insurer_leis <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "facts")) %>%
  filter(country == report_country, concept %in% financial_concepts) %>%
  distinct(lei) %>%
  collect() %>%
  pull(lei)

wanted <- c(unique(measures$measure), paste0(unique(measures$measure), "_prior"))
firms <- values %>%
  select(filing, key, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "key", values_from = "value")
for (k in setdiff(wanted, names(firms))) firms[[k]] <- NA_real_

ratio <- function(a, b) ifelse(!is.na(b) & b > 0, 100 * a / b, NA_real_)
growth <- function(a, b) ifelse(!is.na(b) & b > 0 & !is.na(a), 100 * (a / b - 1), NA_real_)

firms <- primary %>%
  select(lei, filing, fy, period_end) %>%
  inner_join(firms, by = "filing") %>%
  left_join(currency_of, by = "filing") %>%
  left_join(issuer_names, by = "lei") %>%
  group_by(lei) %>%
  mutate(financial = lei %in% insurer_leis |
           any(!is.na(interest) & interest > 0 &
                 (is.na(revenue) | interest >= bank_interest_share * revenue))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(dividends = abs(dividends), dividends_prior = abs(dividends_prior),
         op_margin = ratio(operating, revenue),
         net_margin = ratio(profit, revenue),
         equity_ratio = ratio(equity, assets),
         roe = ratio(profit, equity),
         roa = ratio(profit, assets),
         revenue_growth = growth(revenue, revenue_prior),
         loss = profit < 0,
         in_sum = currency == sum_currency)

# A listed holding and its listed subsidiary both report the same group:
# Heineken Holding consolidates Heineken, ING Groep consolidates ING Bank.
# Two reports of one year whose total assets agree to within
# `twin_tolerance`, whose revenue does too where both state one, and whose
# equity agrees to within `twin_equity_tolerance`, are taken to be one
# group. The one with the larger equity -- the holding,
# which carries the other's minorities -- stays in every sum, and the other
# is shown in the tables and marked, but counted once.
twins <- firms %>%
  filter(!is.na(assets), assets > 0) %>%
  select(fy, currency, lei, issuer, assets, revenue, equity) %>%
  inner_join(., ., by = c("fy", "currency"), suffix = c("", "_other"),
             relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  filter(lei != lei_other,
         abs(assets / assets_other - 1) < twin_tolerance,
         !is.na(equity), !is.na(equity_other), equity_other != 0,
         abs(equity / equity_other - 1) < twin_equity_tolerance,
         (is.na(revenue) & is.na(revenue_other)) |
           (!is.na(revenue) & !is.na(revenue_other) & revenue_other != 0 &
              abs(revenue / revenue_other - 1) < twin_tolerance),
         coalesce(equity, -Inf) < coalesce(equity_other, -Inf) |
           (coalesce(equity, -Inf) == coalesce(equity_other, -Inf) &
              lei > lei_other)) %>%
  distinct(fy, lei, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(fy, lei, twin = issuer_other)

firms <- firms %>%
  left_join(twins, by = c("fy", "lei")) %>%
  mutate(in_sum = in_sum & is.na(twin),
         label = ifelse(is.na(twin), issuer, paste0(issuer, " ²")))

corporates <- firms %>% filter(!financial)
financials <- firms %>% filter(financial)

if (nrow(corporates) == 0) {
  stop("No report of ", report_country, " in the years shown carries a ",
       "figure this factsheet reads.")
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The year by year
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# A like-for-like change: the sum over the issuers that state both years of
# the figure in one report, this year's against the year before's.
lfl <- function(data, key) {
  prior <- paste0(key, "_prior")
  d <- data[!is.na(data[[key]]) & !is.na(data[[prior]]) & data$in_sum, ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0 || sum(d[[prior]]) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  100 * (sum(d[[key]]) / sum(d[[prior]]) - 1)
}
lfl_n <- function(data, key) {
  prior <- paste0(key, "_prior")
  sum(!is.na(data[[key]]) & !is.na(data[[prior]]) & data$in_sum)
}
q <- function(x, p) if (sum(!is.na(x)) >= 3) unname(quantile(x, p, na.rm = TRUE)) else NA_real_

by_year <- corporates %>%
  filter(is.na(twin)) %>%
  group_by(fy) %>%
  group_modify(~ tibble(
    issuers = nrow(.x),
    with_revenue = sum(!is.na(.x$revenue)),
    revenue_sum = sum(.x$revenue[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    operating_sum = sum(.x$operating[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    profit_sum = sum(.x$profit[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    assets_sum = sum(.x$assets[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    ocf_sum = sum(.x$ocf[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    dividends_sum = sum(.x$dividends[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    cash_sum = sum(.x$cash[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    staff_sum = sum(.x$staff[.x$in_sum], na.rm = TRUE),
    revenue_lfl = lfl(.x, "revenue"),
    revenue_lfl_n = lfl_n(.x, "revenue"),
    operating_lfl = lfl(.x, "operating"),
    profit_lfl = lfl(.x, "profit"),
    staff_lfl = lfl(.x, "staff"),
    growth_median = q(.x$revenue_growth, .5),
    op_margin_median = q(.x$op_margin, .5),
    net_margin_median = q(.x$net_margin, .5),
    equity_ratio_median = q(.x$equity_ratio, .5),
    roe_median = q(.x$roe, .5),
    loss_share = 100 * mean(.x$loss, na.rm = TRUE),
    growing_share = 100 * mean(.x$revenue_growth > 0, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup()

latest <- corporates %>% filter(fy == latest_year)
latest_fin <- financials %>% filter(fy == latest_year)
ly <- by_year %>% filter(fy == latest_year)
py <- by_year %>% filter(fy == latest_year - 1)

# Whether the latest year is still being filed, which every figure of it
# has to be read against: a sum over two-thirds of the issuers is not a fall.
n_latest <- nrow(latest)
n_before <- sum(corporates$fy == latest_year - 1)
partial <- n_before > 0 && n_latest < 0.9 * n_before
```

```{r title, results='asis'}
# The title of the document, which a screen reader announces and PDF/UA
# requires.
typst_document_title(paste0("ESEF economic factsheet, ", Country_name,
                            ", financial years ", period_range))
```

```{r formats}
fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  x <- ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 / 10^digits, 0, x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",",
                 decimal.mark = "."))
}
fmt_signed <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–", paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""), fmt(x, digits)))
}
bn <- function(x) fmt(x / 1e9, 1)
mn <- function(x) fmt(x / 1e6, 0)
wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 125) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}
source_caption <- caption_corporate_design(
  source = "ESEF annual financial reports, filings.xbrl.org; fincommons esef module.",
  lang = "en")
typst_string <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  gsub("\"", "\\\\\"", x)
}
ts <- function(x) {
  x <- ifelse(is.na(x), "–", as.character(x))
  paste0("\"", typst_string(x), "\"")
}

# A table written as Typst rather than as a Markdown table, which gives the
# columns the widths they need instead of the ones Pandoc guesses.
typst_table <- function(df, widths, align, size = 7.5, groups = NULL) {
  cells <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) {
    row <- paste(ts(unlist(df[i, ], use.names = FALSE)), collapse = ", ")
    if (!is.null(groups) && !is.na(groups[i]) && nzchar(groups[i])) {
      row <- paste0("table.cell(colspan: ", ncol(df),
                    ", inset: (top: 7pt, bottom: 3pt, x: 4pt), text(weight: \"bold\", ",
                    ts(groups[i]), ")), ", row)
    }
    row
  }, character(1))
  paste0(
    "\n```{=typst}\n#block(width: 100%, text(size: ", size, "pt, {\n",
    "set par(justify: false)\ntable(\n",
    "  columns: (", paste(widths, collapse = ", "), "),\n",
    "  align: (", paste(align, collapse = ", "), "),\n",
    "  inset: (x: 4pt, y: 2.8pt),\n",
    "  stroke: (x, y) => if y == 0 { (top: 0.7pt + rgb(\"#22282E\"), ",
    "bottom: 0.4pt + rgb(\"#22282E\")) } else { none },\n",
    "  table.header(", paste0("text(weight: \"bold\", ", ts(names(df)), ")",
                             collapse = ", "), "),\n  ",
    paste(cells, collapse = ",\n  "),
    ",\n  table.hline(stroke: 0.7pt + rgb(\"#22282E\"))\n)}))\n```\n\n")
}

cols <- design_colours()
year_cols <- as.character(report_years)
```

```{r cover, results='asis'}
title <- paste("Listed companies in", country_name)
subtitle <- paste0("Recent facts and trends from their annual financial ",
                   "reports, financial years ", period_range)

tile <- function(value, label, colour) {
  paste0("box(width: 100%, inset: (x: 8pt, y: 7pt), stroke: (left: 2pt + rgb(\"",
         colour, "\")), [#text(size: 17pt, weight: \"bold\", ", ts(value),
         ")\\ #text(size: 7.5pt, fill: rgb(\"#5C666F\"), ", ts(label), ")])")
}

direction <- function(x, up, down) ifelse(is.na(x), "", ifelse(x >= 0, up, down))
change_word <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x)) return("could not be compared")
  paste0(direction(x, "rose by ", "fell by "), fmt(abs(x), 1), " %")
}

top5_share <- {
  d <- latest %>% filter(in_sum, !is.na(revenue)) %>% arrange(desc(revenue))
  if (nrow(d) > 5) 100 * sum(head(d$revenue, 5)) / sum(d$revenue) else NA_real_
}

  paste0("**Profits.** Operating profit ", change_word(ly$operating_lfl),

         else "", "."),
  paste0("**Margins.** The median operating margin is ",

         if (nrow(py) == 1) paste0(" (", fmt(py$op_margin_median, 1), " % in ",
                                   latest_year - 1, ")") else "",
         ", the median return on equity ", fmt(ly$roe_median, 1), " %."),
  paste0("**Balance sheets.** The median equity ratio is ",

  if (!is.na(top5_share)) paste0("**Concentration.** The five largest ",
         "companies account for ", fmt(top5_share), " % of the revenue of all ",

## The trend

```{r trend-alt}
# The data of the chart below and its alt text, which the options of the
# chunk that draws it read, and so are computed before it.
trend <- by_year %>%
  select(fy, Revenue = revenue_lfl, `Operating profit` = operating_lfl,
         `Result for the year` = profit_lfl) %>%
  pivot_longer(-fy, names_to = "what", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(what = factor(what, levels = c("Revenue", "Operating profit",
                                        "Result for the year")),
         fy = factor(fy))
alt_trend <- if (nrow(trend) == 0) {
  "No chart: no like-for-like change could be computed for any year."
} else {
  paste0("Bar chart in three panels, revenue, operating profit and the result for the ",
         "year, each with one bar per financial year showing the like-for-like change on ",
         "the year before in per cent, for the companies other than banks and insurers. ",
         paste(vapply(levels(droplevels(trend$what)), function(w) {
           d <- trend %>% filter(what == w)
           paste0(w, ": ", paste(d$fy, paste0(fmt_signed(d$value), " %"), collapse = ", "))
         }, character(1)), collapse = "; "), ".")
}
```

```{r trend-chart}
#| fig-height: 2.5
#| fig-alt: !expr alt_trend
# One panel per measure rather than three bars side by side in a colour
# each, so that a bar is told what it measures by the title of its panel
# and not by its colour alone. The fills stay, and are colours that stand
# out from the page.
temp <- trend
ggplot(temp, aes(x = fy, y = value, fill = what)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_signed(value),
                vjust = ifelse(value >= 0, -0.35, 1.25)),
            size = 2.5, colour = cols[["ink"]]) +
  geom_zeroline() +
  facet_wrap(~what, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(cols[["blue"]], palette_accessible[2], cols[["teal"]])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) fmt(x), expand = expansion(mult = .15)) +
  labs(subtitle = paste("Change on the year before, like for like, %;",
                        "companies other than banks and insurers"),
       caption = wrap_caption(source_caption)) +
  theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size,
                         axis.title = element_blank())

```{r margin-alt}
margins <- corporates %>%
  select(fy, `Operating margin` = op_margin, `Net margin` = net_margin,
         `Return on equity` = roe, `Equity ratio` = equity_ratio) %>%
  pivot_longer(-fy, names_to = "what", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  group_by(what, fy) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  summarise(q1 = quantile(value, .25), median = median(value),
            q3 = quantile(value, .75), .groups = "drop")
alt_margin <- if (nrow(margins) == 0) {
  "No chart: too few companies state the figures for a median."
} else {
  paste0("Line charts in four panels, operating margin, net margin, return on equity and ",
         "equity ratio, each showing the median across the companies by financial year in ",
         "per cent, with the interquartile range as a shaded band. ",
         paste(vapply(intersect(c("Operating margin", "Net margin", "Return on equity",
                                  "Equity ratio"), margins$what), function(w) {
           d <- margins %>% filter(what == w) %>% arrange(fy)
           paste0(w, ", median: ", paste(d$fy, fmt(d$median, 1), collapse = ", "),
                  " (", max(d$fy), " quartiles ", fmt(d$q1[nrow(d)], 1), " to ",
                  fmt(d$q3[nrow(d)], 1), ")")
         }, character(1)), collapse = "; "), ".")
}

## The movers

```{r movers, results='asis'}
eligible <- latest %>%
  filter(!is.na(revenue_growth), !is.na(revenue_prior),
         revenue_prior >= movers_min_revenue)
mover_table <- function(d) {
  d %>% transmute(Company = label,
                  `Revenue, m` = paste(currency, mn(revenue)),
                  `Year before, m` = mn(revenue_prior),
                  `Growth, %` = fmt_signed(revenue_growth),
                  `Op. margin, %` = fmt(op_margin, 1))
}
if (nrow(eligible) >= 4) {
  up <- eligible %>% arrange(desc(revenue_growth)) %>% head(movers_n)
  down <- eligible %>% arrange(revenue_growth) %>% head(movers_n) %>%
    filter(!lei %in% up$lei)
  cat("### Fastest growing\n\n")
  cat(typst_table(mover_table(up), widths = c("1fr", rep("auto", 4)),
                  align = c("left", rep("right", 4))))
  cat("### Largest declines\n\n")
  cat(typst_table(mover_table(down), widths = c("1fr", rep("auto", 4)),
                  align = c("left", rep("right", 4))))
  cat(paste0("Companies with revenue of at least ", fmt(movers_min_revenue / 1e6),
             " million in their own currency the year before, ", latest_year,
             " against ", latest_year - 1, " as stated in the ", latest_year,
             " report. A large change is as often an acquisition, a disposal or ",
             "a change of what is consolidated as it is trade.\n"))
} else {
  cat("Too few companies report revenue for two years to name movers.\n")
}
```

    arrange(desc(currency == sum_currency), desc(assets)) %>%
    transmute(Company = label,
              `Total assets, m` = trimws(paste(ifelse(currency == sum_currency, "", currency),
                                               mn(assets))),
              `Equity ratio, %` = fmt(equity_ratio, 1),
              `Result, m` = mn(profit),
              `Year before, m` = mn(profit_prior),
              `ROE, %` = fmt(roe, 1),
              `ROA, %` = fmt(roa, 2))
  names(temp)[2] <- paste0("Total assets, ", sum_currency, " m")
  cat(typst_table(temp, widths = c("1fr", rep("auto", 6)),
                  align = c("left", rep("right", 6)), size = 7))
  fin_lfl <- lfl(latest_fin, "profit")
  cat(paste0("A company is counted as a bank where its interest revenue ",
             "under the effective interest method is at least ",
             fmt(bank_interest_share * 100), " % of its revenue, or where it ",
             "tags no revenue at all, and as an insurer where it presents a ",
             "line of IFRS 17. ",
             "The result of those reporting both years ",
             change_word(fin_lfl), " like for like. ",
             "A group whose bank is a small part of it stays among the ",
             "companies.", twin_note(latest_fin), "\n"))
}
```

## How the figures are put together

```{r method, results='asis'}
cov <- filings %>%
  filter(fy %in% report_years) %>%
  group_by(fy) %>%
  summarise(listed = n(), read = sum(read), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(firms %>% group_by(fy) %>%
              summarise(companies = sum(!financial), financial = sum(financial),
                        other_ccy = sum(!in_sum, na.rm = TRUE),
                        .groups = "drop"), by = "fy") %>%
  left_join(corporates %>% group_by(fy) %>%
              summarise(revenue = sum(!is.na(revenue)),
                        ifrs15 = sum(filing %in% basis$filing[basis$measure == "revenue" & basis$rank == 2]),
                        .groups = "drop"), by = "fy")
temp <- cov %>% transmute(`Financial year` = as.character(fy),
                          `Reports listed` = fmt(listed),
                          `With facts` = fmt(read),
                          Companies = fmt(companies),
                          `Banks, insurers` = fmt(financial),
                          `With revenue` = fmt(revenue),
                          other = fmt(other_ccy))
names(temp)[7] <- paste0("Not in ", sum_currency)
cat(typst_table(temp,
                widths = c("1fr", rep("auto", 6)),
                align = c("left", rep("right", 6))))
notes <- c(
  paste0("**What it reads.** The tables of filings and facts of the `esef` ",
         "module of fincommons: the annual financial reports that issuers ",
         "of ", country_name, " with securities on a regulated market file ",
         "in the European Single Electronic Format, as collected by ",
         "filings.xbrl.org. That is listed companies and issuers of listed ",
         "bonds, not the economy as a whole: no private company and no ",
         "public body is in it."),
  paste0("**Which report.** One per company and financial year: where a year ",
         "was filed more than once -- a correction, a second language -- the ",
         "report with the most facts. A financial year ending on or before ",
         "30 June is counted as the year before."),
  paste0("**Which figures.** Only figures of the group as a whole, with no ",
         "breakdown, for the twelve months or the balance-sheet date of the ",
         "report. Revenue is IFRS revenue, or IFRS 15 revenue where that is ",
         "all a report tags; the result is the total, or the parent's share ",
         "where that is all; likewise equity. Ratios are of figures from the ",
         "same report: operating and net margin on revenue, return on equity ",
         "and the equity ratio on year-end equity and assets. A ratio over a ",
         "denominator of zero or less is left out."),
  paste0("**What is left out.** Banks and insurers from every corporate ",
         "figure. A group reported both by a listed holding and by its listed ",
         "subsidiary is counted once in every sum and median", if (nrow(twins) > 0)
         paste0(" (", paste(unique(paste(firms$issuer[!is.na(firms$twin)], "under",
                                          firms$twin[!is.na(firms$twin)])),
                            collapse = "; "), ")") else "",
         "; one consolidated into another only in part is not found and is ",
         "counted twice. ", if (nrow(identity) > 0) paste0(
         fmt(n_distinct(identity$filing)), " report", if (n_distinct(identity$filing) == 1) "" else "s",
         " that name", if (n_distinct(identity$filing) == 1) "s" else "",
         " another entity than the one ",
         "of the LEI ", if (n_distinct(identity$filing) == 1) "it is" else "they are",
         " filed under (", paste(unique(substr(identity$stated, 1, 40)), collapse = "; "),
         "): a filing agent's test report or a report filed under the wrong ",
         "LEI, whose figures are either not real or counted already. ") else "",
         " A company that does not tag a line from every sum and ",
         "median of that line -- the data quality factsheet of the same ",
         "country says which issuers tag little. Nothing is converted between ",
         "currencies."),
  paste0("This factsheet is produced by a template of the open-source ",
         "project fincommons. It reads a public record, is given without ",
         "warranty as to correctness or completeness, and carries no ",
         "association with the issuers, with XBRL International or with ESMA. ",
         "It is not investment advice."))
cat(paste(notes, collapse = "\n\n"))
```
